criterion: Study status is explicit and claims match it
guiding_question: Does the paper state whether it reports a plan or proposal or completed empirical work, and are its claims consistent with that status?
score_0_anchor: Status is not stated, or planned or untested work is presented as a result or as validated.
score_1_anchor: Status is stated, but at least one claim exceeds it (for example, an untested method called effective, or preliminary data cited without a method).
score_2_anchor: Status is stated in the title, abstract, or method; every result claim is backed by reported work; and future work is labelled as future.

criterion: Outcome metrics are reported in a form that supports comparison
guiding_question: Are outcome or performance metrics named, operationalized, and reported (or, for a plan, specified) in enough detail for another study to compare against?
score_0_anchor: No outcome metric is named, or results are given only as qualitative impressions.
score_1_anchor: Metrics are named, but at least one lacks a definition, unit, scale, or aggregation rule, or the values needed for comparison (per item or per condition) are not reported.
score_2_anchor: Every outcome metric is defined with its unit or scale and computation, and values (or, for a plan, the planned report format) are given per condition in a comparable form.

criterion: Improvement claims are tested against a specified baseline
guiding_question: If the paper claims or implies improvement over an alternative or current practice, does it compare against a stated and specified baseline? NA allowed if the paper makes no improvement or superiority claim.
score_0_anchor: Improvement is claimed or implied but no baseline or comparator is used or planned.
score_1_anchor: A baseline is named but not specified enough to reproduce, or conditions differ between the compared arms.
score_2_anchor: A specified baseline is compared under matched conditions (same tasks and data), and the comparison is reported or planned for each outcome.

criterion: Quality tasks are defined for each phase in scope
guiding_question: If the paper proposes or applies a QA or quality process, does it define, for each phase in scope, what task is done, when, by whom, and with what output? NA allowed if no QA or quality process is proposed or applied.
score_0_anchor: Phases or quality tasks are not defined, or are named only as goals.
score_1_anchor: Phases are defined, but at least one in-scope phase lacks its task, trigger or timing, responsible role, or output.
score_2_anchor: Every in-scope phase states its task, trigger or timing, responsible role, and output artifact.

criterion: Validation method is stated and matches each claim
guiding_question: Is a validation or evaluation method stated for each main claim, with its procedure and sample, and does the method test what the claim states?
score_0_anchor: No validation or evaluation method is stated for the main claims.
score_1_anchor: A method is stated, but the procedure or sample is missing for at least one claim, or at least one conclusion rests on an aspect the method did not directly test.
score_2_anchor: Each main claim has a stated method with procedure and sample, and each conclusion is limited to what that method tested.
source_location: A: Abstract; §4.2 paras 1-3. B: p. 61 Research Methods

criterion: Bias threats in the evaluation design are controlled
guiding_question: Does the evaluation design name specific bias threats (for example, order, learning, priming, group influence) and a concrete control for each?
score_1_anchor: Some controls are described, but at least one evident threat in the design is unaddressed, or a control is unspecified (for example, a sufficient gap with no duration).
score_2_anchor: Each evident design threat is named with a concrete control (for example, counterbalanced order, neutral moderator, open questions before closed questions).
source_location: A: §4.2 para 3. B: p. 65 Construct Validity

criterion: Each research question traces to variables and data sources
guiding_question: Is each research question linked to the variables or hypotheses it examines and to the data source used to answer it?
score_0_anchor: Research questions are absent, or no link to variables or data is given.
score_1_anchor: Some research questions are linked, or links lack either the variable or hypothesis or the data source.
score_2_anchor: Every research question is linked to its variables or hypotheses and to its data source (for example in a table).
source_location: A: §4.1. B: p. 60 Research Questions; p. 62 Table 1

criterion: Feasibility, effort, and acceptance are assessed separately
guiding_question: When a method or process is evaluated, are feasibility (can it be done), effort (benefit versus cost), and acceptance (will users adopt it) posed as separate questions with separate evidence? NA allowed if the paper does not evaluate a method or process intended for adoption.
score_0_anchor: None of the three is assessed, or they are merged into a single works-well judgment.
score_1_anchor: One or two of the three are assessed separately, or all three are named but share undifferentiated evidence.
score_2_anchor: All three are posed as distinct questions, each with its own evidence and conclusion.
source_location: p. 60 Research Questions and Feasibility; p. 62 Table 1 legend

criterion: Acceptance is measured with defined constructs
guiding_question: If user or developer acceptance is assessed, is it measured with defined constructs (for example, perceived usefulness, ease of use, intention to use) and a stated instrument? NA allowed if acceptance is neither assessed nor claimed.
score_0_anchor: Acceptance is claimed or planned without named constructs or instrument.
score_1_anchor: Constructs are named, but the instrument, scale, or aggregation is not stated.
score_2_anchor: Named constructs are measured with a stated instrument and scale, and results are reported per construct.
source_location: pp. 60-61 Acceptance; p. 64 Acceptance of Desk-Checking

criterion: Participants, data, and setting are described
guiding_question: Are the participants, data, or study setting described well enough (who, how many, experience, selection) to judge to whom the results apply?
score_0_anchor: Participants or data are not described.
score_1_anchor: Some descriptors are given (for example, role), but count, experience, or selection is missing.
score_2_anchor: Count, relevant experience or characteristics, and selection or setting are all stated.

criterion: Analysis and aggregation procedure is recomputable
guiding_question: Is the analysis or aggregation procedure stated for each data type so that another reviewer could recompute the reported results from the data?
score_1_anchor: A procedure is stated for some data types only, or is named without the rule needed to recompute (for example, analyzed and compared).
score_2_anchor: Each data type has a stated procedure with its decision rules (for example, median with tie rule, or coding then counting).
source_location: A: §4.2 para 1; §4.2 para 3. B: p. 61 Research Methods

criterion: Evidence is protected by validity safeguards
guiding_question: Does the study use and report safeguards that make its evidence checkable (for example, triangulation, chain of evidence, member checking, independent review of steps)?
score_1_anchor: One safeguard is used or implied (for example, multiple data sources) but is not tied to a validity aim.
score_2_anchor: Two or more safeguards are reported and each is tied to the validity aspect it protects.

criterion: Threats and limits of the method are reported and carried into conclusions
guiding_question: Does the paper report threats to validity and the limits of its own method, and are its conclusions qualified accordingly?
score_0_anchor: No limitations or threats are reported and conclusions are unqualified.
score_1_anchor: Limits are reported, but at least one limit of the method stated elsewhere in the paper is not carried into the conclusions.
score_2_anchor: Threats are reported by type, include limits of the method itself, and every conclusion is qualified by them.
source_location: p. 65 Construct Validity; pp. 65-66 External Validity

criterion: Variability coverage of the results is stated
guiding_question: Does the paper state which configurations, settings, datasets, or variants its results cover, and which they do not?
score_0_anchor: No statement of the configurations or settings covered.
score_1_anchor: Scope is stated at a general level (domain or single setting), but the covered variants or settings are not enumerated, or no exclusion is stated.
score_2_anchor: Covered variants or settings (for example, tasks, datasets, hyperparameters, environments) are enumerated, and at least one exclusion or untested variant is named.
source_location: B: p. 59 Case Study Background; p. 63 Advantages of Variability Modeling; p. 64 para 1. A: §5 para 1

criterion: Authors report a self-review pass of their own artifacts
guiding_question: Do the authors report a review pass of their own study artifacts (instruments, code, data, analysis) before use or release, and state what it checked? NA allowed if the paper produces and plans no study artifacts.
score_0_anchor: No review of the study's own artifacts is reported.
score_1_anchor: A review is mentioned without stating what was checked or by whom.
score_2_anchor: A review pass is reported with what was checked (for example, questionnaire understandability, each analysis step) and who checked it.
source_location: p. 59 Review; p. 60 para 3; p. 63 sidebar Proposed Desk-Checking Checklist; p. 65 Construct Validity; p. 66 Reliability
